docMeta.dd: Exhaustion is not a status symbol

source.excerpt:
Lillian Cunningham: You have a quote in your book, “One of the most universal numbing strategies is what I call ‘crazy-busy.’” Elaborate on this concept.

Brené Brown: ‘Crazy-busy’ is a great armor, it’s a great way for numbing. What a lot of us do is that we stay so busy, and so out in front of our life, that the truth of how we’re feeling and what we really need can’t catch up with us.
trail: The line reads like speech, and it is. Her interviewer opens by quoting Daring Greatly — “One of the most universal numbing strategies is what I call ‘crazy-busy’” — and asks Brown to elaborate; her answer is the famous sentence. The archived transcript ↗

The exchange ran in the Post’s On Leadership section under the headline “Exhaustion is not a status symbol,” bylined Lillian Cunningham, with the paper’s own publication stamp reading 3 October 2012. Archived page one ↗
Wikiquote lists the sentence in its sourced Quotes section with the same origin — Washington Post, October 2012 — and Quote Investigator has never had cause to open a file on it. Wikiquote ↗
source.excerptNote: The piece ran as an edited transcript of a conversation. The question quotes Daring Greatly; Brown’s spoken answer is the sentence that now circulates on its own.

author.metaLine: Born 18 November 1965 · American research professor & author on shame and vulnerability
author.bio: Brené Brown is an American research professor who holds the Huffington Foundation’s Brené Brown Endowed Chair at the University of Houston’s Graduate College of Social Work, and is a visiting professor in management at the McCombs School of Business. Her work on shame, vulnerability and courage reached a mass audience after a widely viewed 2010 TED talk, and she has since written six number-one New York Times bestsellers, among them The Gifts of Imperfection, Daring Greatly and Atlas of the Heart. When she gave the 2012 interview that produced this line, Daring Greatly was her latest book.

context.heading: Why it landed
lead: The Post’s On Leadership section framed the conversation around overwork: why does everyone feel permanently behind? Brown’s answer reframed busyness as a defence mechanism rather than a scheduling problem — armour worn to keep your own feelings at arm’s length. The interview ↗ ran under the headline “Exhaustion is not a status symbol,” which took on a life of its own alongside the quotation.

The idea came out of Daring Greatly, where Brown catalogues the “shields” people raise against vulnerability and names numbing as one of them. The interviewer read the book’s line back to her — “One of the most universal numbing strategies is what I call ‘crazy-busy’” — and it was Brown’s spoken elaboration, not the book sentence, that became the quotation people share.
context.detailsSummary: Why you won’t find this line in the book
detailsBody: Search Daring Greatly for this sentence and it isn’t there. The book’s wording is the one the interviewer quotes in her question: “One of the most universal numbing strategies is what I call ‘crazy-busy.’” The famous version — the armour, the truth that can’t catch up with us — is what Brown said next, in conversation. That is why it reads like speech rather than prose.
context.pull: “Exhaustion is not a status symbol” — the Post’s headline over the interview

sourcesVerified.claim: Contains, verbatim, Brown's answer "'Crazy-busy' is a great armor, it's a great way for numbing. What a lot of us do is that we stay so busy, and so out in front of our life, that the truth of how we're feeling and what we really need can't catch up with us." and the preceding question quoting Daring Greatly's line "One of the most universal numbing strategies is what I call 'crazy-busy.'"

The article is headlined "Exhaustion is not a status symbol," bylined Lillian Cunningham / The Washington Post, appears in the On Leadership section, carries the publication stamp 10/03/2012, and describes itself as "this edited transcript of our conversation" with University of Houston professor Brené Brown about her latest book, Daring Greatly.

Wikiquote's sourced Quotes section for Brené Brown lists this quotation first, cited to Washington Post, October 2012, and states she was born 18 November 1965, holds the Huffington Foundation's Brené Brown Endowed Chair at the University of Houston, is a visiting professor at McCombs, became famous after a 2010 TED talk, and has written six number-one New York Times bestsellers.

Wikipedia gives her full name as Casandra Brené Brown, born 18 November 1965 in San Antonio, Texas; the Huffington Foundation Brené Brown Endowed Chair at the University of Houston's Graduate College of Social Work; visiting professor in management at the McCombs School of Business; and Daring Greatly published 2012 by Gotham.
A-Z Quotes carries the quotation with the source line: "Exhaustion is not a status symbol" by Lillian Cunningham, www.washingtonpost.com, October 3, 2012.
The Minds Journal reproduces the quotation attributed to Brené Brown with no original publication, interview, date or link given.

This page renders the quotation as "Crazy busy is a great armor, it's a great way for numbing... so out front of our life..." — dropping the quotation marks and hyphen around 'Crazy-busy' and the word "in" from "out in front of our life" — credited only to "Brene Brown".
